description: issue #768, the BOOLEAN half of what the ruling newly rejects: `spec/interaction-events.md:129`/`:131` — the prompt MUST be a `word`, and anything else raises `ol-type`. Paired with `input-prompt-number-rejected`, this pins BOTH scalars that #681 previously accepted, which is what makes the ruling's narrowing observable rather than a comment: an implementation still carrying #681's scalar reading passes every other fixture in this directory and fails exactly these two. `boolean` is worth its own fixture rather than folding into the number case because it is the kind whose printed form (`true`) reads most like an ordinary prompt word, so it is the likeliest to be waved through by an implementation that classifies by appearance instead of by type. The `instruction` event is emitted first (seq 0) and the check fails before the read, so no `primitive` event is emitted and nothing is printed; the scripted answer stays unconsumed, which is also what distinguishes this from the read's cancelled ending (`input-unanswered-cancels`).

diagnostics.message: input needs a prompt word, but got a boolean.
